:::{#def-joint-density-mass}
#### Joint density-mass function

Let $X$ be a discrete random variable and $Y$ a continuous random variable,
[jointly distributed](#def-jointly-distributed).
A **joint density-mass function** of $X$ and $Y$,
denoted $\p(X = x,\, Y = y)$,
is a function $\p(X = x,\, Y = y) \ge 0$
that is a probability mass in $x$ and a probability density in $y$:
for every $x$ and every set $B \subseteq \reals$,

$$\Pr(X = x,\, Y \in B) = \int_{B} \p(X = x,\, Y = y)\,dy$$

:::
